criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Strong frames: 1, a lit 6061 part with two shadowed pockets in the vise, end mill held clear, coolant hoses, raking key. 9, empty bays at standing eye in comal-lit tape with levelling plates, a person for scale and four lit Lockheed enclosures beyond. 6, 24 cyan outlines beside the 100 roofs at one pitch, the clearest explanatory image in the deck. 4 is a decent spatial frame: two rows receding, a floor pool, a kit machinist for scale, though its machines read closer to vending cabinets than machining centres. Several frames do not reach the 7 descriptor. 2 reads at 432 px as a grey tile grid with a sunken grey tray, the fresh pour carries no light of its own and the rolled carpet corner is a sliver. 3 is 312 identical tiny rectangles that read as a keyboard or server faceplate texture, and the lifted part at top right is about 50 px. 7 is a flat cyanotype wireframe with the part dropped on it. 8 is a primitive slab pendant with toy keys on a flat navy wall. 5 leaves the right half as empty black. The deck is dark and bold rather than faded, which keeps it off the 4 descriptor. Four frames lean on a primitive or a texture, not one.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: Clearly one deck. One machine shop world with a warm low key and near-black fields, and one cyan accent reserved for Hadrian on 6, 7 and 9. Two continuity devices work. The part motif runs 1 to 3 to 7 to absent on 9. The 5 to 6 hold adds only the cell, so the swipe performs the turn. Value stays dark with no strobing. Two frames sit outside. On 8 the field goes saturated navy against the warm graphite of 1 and 4, and 7's blueprint blue is a second cold field. The deck also alternates spatial and plan reliefs, so the camera move is declared more than felt.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every slide numeral traces to figures.json or a claim quote: 735,000, 100,000 and 85,000 to c1 and c2, 250,000 and 800 to c12, 30 to c10, 100 to c11, 24 and 2027 to c4, 2,000 to c5. 2026 is in c11's quote. On 2 the square sides check at one scale. On 3, 13 rows of 24 match parts_per_employee 312, hedged with 'about'. Slide 7's verbatim matches c20. Dallas County comes from the TDLR filing (c34). Looser spots: (1) The caption says 'Hadrian calls its own factories AI powered'. The cited c15 says factories that 'combine ... AI', and the exact 'AI-powered factories' phrasing is c24, whose source is not listed in first_comment.txt. It was fetched, so this is not a hard fail. (2) Slides 7 and 8 scope Opus to 'its own factories' while omitting c22, Hadrian's own page offering manufacturing cells 'deployed in either Hadrian facilities or customer sites'. (3) The cover's 'due in 2027' is firmer than 'expected to be operational in early 2027', though the dek corrects it. Every source is primary corporate or official, so these are phrasing looseness, not fabrication.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A reader learns that Lockheed is putting $300 million into Grand Prairie, that Hadrian's 24-machine cell is expected in early 2027 and will be run by Lockheed's crews, and that the release does not say what AI does there. The deck never says what the plant makes. c7, verified, says Grand Prairie supports PAC-3 MSE, THAAD, PrSM and JATM, so '250,000 parts in 2025' on slide 3 is 250,000 of nothing in particular, and the AI question floats free of what is being built. No public body, no decision a Texan can weigh in on and no next step appear. The one human stake, 2,000 Texas jobs, sits in the last dek of slide 9. The county is named only in the caption.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover's 'A 24 machine cell, due in 2027' is accurate and weak as a hook. Frames 2 to 5 are four consecutive scale counts. 3 is cuttable, and 2 and 3 both delay the cell. The turn at 6 is well built: the same bench with the empty bays added. 7 and 8 land the AI question. 9 closes on 'Lockheed's own crews will run it', which is softer than the question 8 just asked, so the deck peaks one frame early.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean, careful, on house rules. 'The release gives AI no job description' is a good line. 'Drawn to illustrate.' closes eight of nine deks. Process sentences such as 'The block draws 100, at one scale' and 'Each area is drawn as a square at one scale, not the plant's shape' talk about the drawing, not Grand Prairie. There is little regional texture beyond the city name.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The machine shop world and the cyanotype page are new to the window. The structure repeats the last two decks: no. 54 set a counted block beside the projected plant's slots at the same pitch, and no. 55 set lids in taped bays with a single accent. Here frames 5 and 6 are a 100 block beside 24 taped bays at the same pitch in one accent. The close-crop object cover echoes no. 55's wall camera close.

one_sentence_fix: Say what the plant builds, using verified c7 (components for PAC-3 MSE, THAAD, PrSM and JATM), on the cover dek and on slide 3, so the 250,000 parts, the 24-machine cell and the AI question are about missile production a Texan can picture.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: At feed size it reads as a grey tile grid with a sunken grey tray. The fresh pour has no lit face, the rolled carpet corner is a sliver, and the slab's tile lines turn it into graph paper.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Take the regular grid off the slab and keep only wide-pitch saw joints, give the form boards and the rolled carpet corner long casts, and light the 100,000 pour as the one bright surface against a slab that falls to near black.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: 312 identical tiny parts in flat plan read as a keyboard or rack texture. The lifted part, which carries the unit, is about 50 px and lost at top right.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Move the lifted part and its empty pocket into a foreground pool at least 250 px wide, and delete the second tray below.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The pendant is a primitive rounded slab with toy-block keys on a flat saturated navy wall. The background breaks the deck's warm graphite world.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Replace the navy wall with the graphite enclosure and its shut door's lit window falling to black. Model a bevelled housing with an e-stop, recessed keys and a knurled handwheel. Rake the keys from the left.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A flat cyanotype wireframe that reads as a UI mockup. The part sits on it with almost no cast, and machine_qa flags a weak lower zone.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Enlarge the part to about half the sheet width and set it in the lower third with a long cast across the linework, and let black granite show around the sheet's edges.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The right half of the frame is empty black, a dead zone at feed size, and the roofs read as dominoes more than machines.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Lay a faint, unmarked pool of the low key on the empty floor where frame 6 sets the cell, and strengthen the stack-pole casts down the aisles.
